clue.text: Recall spiel and sell sporting accessory

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the combined words are read backwards here

parts.note: a spiel is glib talk, the gift of the gab
to flog is slang for to sell

explanation.surface: A salesman reminisces about patter and selling some piece of sports kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' turns round the whole of GAB + FLOG, giving GOLF then BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer carries clubs in one, so it is an accessory for that sport.

clue.text: Prophetic judge primarily avoiding jesting about artist

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the artist
avoiding means that letter is left out of the jesting word

parts.note: jocular means jesting, joking

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the word judge

parts.note: first letter of judge
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A judge, avoiding jokes about a painter, makes a solemn pronouncement.
explanation.walkthrough: JOCULAR without J leaves OCULAR; 'about' puts that round RA, giving O + RA + CULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle foretold the future, so oracular speech is prophetic.

clue.text: Body part shown by British runner coming from going uphill

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill reads the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: a miler is a middle-distance runner
of can mean coming from, as in 'a man of Kent'

explanation.surface: A British athlete runs uphill and something is said about a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: B + MILER + OF read upwards gives FO + RELIM + B.
explanation.definitionFit: A forelimb is a front leg or arm of an animal, a part of its anatomy.

clue.text: They advise you against swapping iodine for nitrogen in explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart, so they are rearranged
swapping ... for tells us one element symbol replaces the other in the words you against
for marks the iodine as what the nitrogen stands in for

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Advice warns against swapping chemicals, lest a blast follow.
explanation.walkthrough: YOU AGAINST with its I changed to N gives YOUAGANNST, whose letters 'explosion' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony aunts are newspaper columnists who give readers advice on personal problems.

clue.text: Priest, Greek character religious graduate ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the graduate's letters are left out of the Greek letter

parts.note: lambda is the Greek letter L
BD is a Bachelor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A Greek priest overlooks a theology graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet.

clue.text: Hot lust, perhaps, provided upsetting conclusion

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the pieces upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
lust is one of the seven deadly sins, so an example of sin
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Lust gives an upsetting ending to a passionate affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The finish of something is its end, its conclusion.

clue.text: The least you could expect — silence in one minute? Just the reverse

indicators.note: just the reverse says the pieces named, silence then one then minute, go in the opposite order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mum means silence, as in 'mum's the word'

explanation.surface: A minute's silence is the least you could expect as a mark of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the named pieces in the opposite order gives minute, one, silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the lowest amount acceptable, the least anyone could hope for.

clue.text: American audacity securing elevated target in response to tragedy?

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside

parts.note: sass is American slang for cheek or audacity

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated lifts the word up so it reads backwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or target

explanation.surface: American audacity in pursuing a lofty aim might end in tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: END raised in a down entry becomes DNE, which SASS holds: SA + DNE + SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow or grief is the natural reaction to a tragic event.

clue.text: Pound I contributed to plain area in big church

indicators.note: contributed to means these letters are added into the middle of the plain word

parts.note: basic means plain, without frills
L is the sign for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone gave a pound to a church collection in a plain area.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large Roman-style church given special status by the Pope.

clue.text: Key support returned precisely after expert's brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the expert is placed inside
returned means the phrase for precisely is read backwards

parts.note: to a T means exactly, precisely
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A supporting part comes back exactly once the expert is called in.
explanation.walkthrough: TO A T backwards is TAOT; PRO goes inside it, giving TA + PRO + OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproot is a plant's main root, growing straight down and anchoring it.

clue.text: Father with fiddle, but nothing moves in part of ear

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: moves means the letter for nothing shifts to another spot within the fiddle word

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Dad plays the fiddle but nothing stirs his ear.
explanation.walkthrough: VIOLIN with its O shifted along becomes VILION.
explanation.definitionFit: The pavilion, or pinna, is the outer visible flap of the ear, an anatomical term.

clue.text: Tar assigned to rear of deck produces instrument

parts.note: pitch is a black tarry substance
for can mean assigned to, intended for

indicators.note: rear of points to the last letter of the word deck

parts.note: last letter of deck

explanation.surface: A sailor, a tar, sent to the back of the deck produces an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like a sailor but stands for the sticky substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitchfork is a farm tool, also an old name for a tuning fork, a musical device.

clue.text: Responsible fellow keeping it in line? On the contrary

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within

parts.note: guy means a fellow

indicators.note: in would put it inside line, but the following words flip that
on the contrary reverses the containment, so line goes inside it

explanation.surface: A dutiful fellow keeps everything in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' turns 'it in line' round: L goes in IT to make ILT, which GUY holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be guilty of something is to be to blame for it, culpable.

clue.text: Pursuing something we stock? Hard to get in when the shop's shut

indicators.note: to get in means the letter is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: after means pursuing, chasing
something we stock is ours, belonging to us
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper says that after closing time it is hard to get in to buy their stock.
explanation.definitionFit: After hours means after normal opening times, when business is closed.

clue.text: Studied about my single year to get cash

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word my is read backwards

parts.note: one means single

explanation.surface: A student muses on their one year of earning money.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'read' a subject is the British way of saying you studied it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash available for immediate payment.

clue.text: Song singer initially released gets award

indicators.note: released means that letter is let go from the song

parts.note: a psalm is a sacred song

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word singer

parts.note: first letter of singer

explanation.surface: A singer releases a song and wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm, a palm branch, is a traditional symbol of victory, hence a prize.

clue.text: Judicial group acknowledge point of survey

parts.note: the bench means judges or magistrates collectively
to mark something is to note or acknowledge it

explanation.surface: The judges acknowledge a point in a survey.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveyors cut a benchmark into stone as a fixed reference height for levelling.

clue.text: Goddess embracing limitless Sahara; a vast desert region

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: Kali is the Hindu goddess of destruction

indicators.note: limitless removes the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A goddess embraces the Sahara, a vast desert.
explanation.walkthrough: SAHARA without its ends is AHAR, which KALI holds after KAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is a huge semi-arid sandy area of southern Africa.

clue.text: Spanish city almost entirely enclosed in Latin road

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the road

parts.note: via is Latin for road

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means entirely, as in 'all alone'
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, used on letters

explanation.surface: A Spanish city lies nearly wholly within an old Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL less a letter is AL, and ENC is the letter-writer's short form of enclosed; both go inside VIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a major port city on Spain's eastern coast.

clue.text: Middle-class novel a good laugh, with a degree of reflection?

parts.note: a gas is informal for something very funny, a good laugh
a degree of reflection asks for most of the previous letters, all but the last, mirrored and added on

explanation.surface: A light suburban novel is a good laugh and a little thoughtful.
explanation.walkthrough: A GAS is mirrored without repeating its S, giving a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga saga is a genre of fiction set in comfortable rural English homes, named after the Aga cooking range.

clue.text: Adored absorbing Neruda; extremely gifted

indicators.note: absorbing means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: to dote on is to adore

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters of the word

parts.note: first and last letters of Neruda

explanation.surface: Fans adored the Chilean poet Pablo Neruda, an extremely gifted writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something donated is given away as a gift, so gifted is a synonym.

clue.text: Celebrations not beginning, sadly

indicators.note: not beginning removes the first letter

parts.note: galas are festive celebrations

explanation.surface: The parties never started, unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of sorrow, an equivalent of unfortunately.

clue.text: Lots of people, tense, gripped by grisly spooky tale

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the other word

parts.note: gory means grisly, bloody
hosts means multitudes, lots of people
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Crowds sit tense, held by a gruesome scary story.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost story is a tale of the supernatural meant to frighten.

clue.text: The present cut ends in worst outcome till now

indicators.note: cut means losing its last letter

parts.note: today means the present time

indicators.note: ends in points to the last letters of the next two words

parts.note: last letter of worst
last letter of outcome

explanation.surface: Today's cuts end in the worst result so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to the present moment, so far.

clue.text: Nothing in hair right for complainant

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone complains that nothing is right with their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A moaner is a grumbler, someone who complains.

clue.text: Showed shame while walking over a doctor to achieve success

indicators.note: over means the walking word sits over, around, the other pieces

parts.note: to slink is to move furtively as if ashamed; slunk is its past tense
MD is a Doctor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Someone sidled past a doctor in shame, trying to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A slam dunk, from basketball, is a certain or easy win, a sure triumph.

clue.text: Characters aboard train in Euston Square

indicators.note: characters aboard means letters travelling within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Travellers boarding a train at Euston, a London station, near its square.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three times three, a square number.

clue.text: Small space for leading Conservative in opportunity to improve

indicators.note: for leading means the substitute takes the place of the opening letter

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
an en is a small printer's space

explanation.surface: A small space for a Tory leader gives a chance to get better.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to make it better or increase its quality.

clue.text: Ditching American in accord about temperature? That's welcome

indicators.note: about means going round the other letter
ditching means dropping the letter from the word

parts.note: in accord means agreeing

explanation.surface: Without the Americans, agreement on climate is welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in accord' means AGREEING; less A that is GREEING, round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting is a word or gesture of welcome.

clue.text: Primarily like a song recalled with mostly rich content?

definitions.text: Primarily like a song recalled with mostly rich content?

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of the word like

parts.note: first letter of like

indicators.note: content means the rich piece is contained in the song
recalled means called back, read backwards

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: rich minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Something songlike, remembered with a rich content.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing is expressive and songlike, like a lyric poem.
